title: The visitor
text:
The first time the stranger appeared, Ewa assumed he was lost. It was a grey afternoon in early March, and she was standing at the kitchen window, waiting for the kettle to boil, when she noticed a man in a long dark coat standing at the end of the garden, just beyond the old apple tree. He was not doing anything. He was simply looking at the house.

She watched him for perhaps a minute. Then the kettle clicked off, she turned to pour the water, and when she looked back he was gone.

He returned the following Tuesday, and the Tuesday after that, always at the same time, always in the same place. He never came closer, never tried the gate, never seemed to notice her watching. Her husband, Adam, laughed when she told him. "A birdwatcher," he said. "Or someone from the council, measuring the boundary." But he did not offer to go out and ask.

By the fourth week, Ewa had begun to arrange her afternoons around the visits. She told herself it was caution. She noted the time in a small notebook – 3.40, 3.42, 3.39 – and the weather, and the colour of his scarf, which was the only thing that ever changed. She found herself wondering what he saw when he looked at the house: the peeling paint around the windows, perhaps, or the swing that nobody had used for years, still hanging from the apple tree, moving slightly in the wind.

On the sixth Tuesday, she put on her coat and walked down the garden.

He did not move as she approached. Up close, he was older than she had thought, his face lined and tired, and he was holding something in his gloved hands: a small, faded photograph. He held it out to her without a word.

It showed the same garden, the same apple tree, the same swing – but newer, brighter, and on the swing sat a boy of about six, laughing at whoever held the camera.

"I lived here," the man said at last, in a voice rough from not being used. "Until I was nine. They told me last month that I don't have much time left." He looked past her, at the swing. "I just wanted to see it again."

Ewa stood beside him for a long while. Then she opened the gate.

exercises.answer: Her fear was turning into curiosity.

exercises.prompt: Why did the man come back every week?
exercises.answer: He was ill and wanted to see his childhood home.
